_comment: Reader-need rules for outline_check.py. Regexes match planned H2 titles (lowercased).

required_sections.label: Why it exists or where it fits
Who uses it and how (use cases or limits)

forbidden_sections.label: No generic closing heading (end on a next step)

reminders: Intro sets up the problem before naming the subject. Don't open with the definition.
First H2 delivers the core answer with one concrete example; close by pointing to an Explain It or Guide Me piece.
Skip the 101: start where the subject is used and why its internals matter now.
Show the mechanism with a diagram, code, a worked example or real numbers; give each component its own section.
Don't give the verdict in the intro: make clear the right choice depends on the reader's needs.
Introduce the comparison table before it and interpret it after it; never call one option universally better.

required_sections.label: Prerequisites first
required_sections.match: prerequisite|requirements|before you (start|begin)|what you('ll)? need|setup|set up your

reminders: Intro says what the reader will have at the end and roughly how long it takes.
One heading per major step, minor steps numbered; show the expected output after key steps.

required_sections.label: Where to get help if nothing works

reminders: One section per fix, from most likely or easiest to rarest; numbered steps with the expected result.
Calm, plain language: the reader is frustrated.
Intro states the surprising result or tension concretely.
Separate what the data shows from opinion; end with how to reproduce the result.

required_sections.label: What it means for the reader
required_sections.match: mean|affect|impact|why it matters|should you|what to do

reminders: Lead with what happened, when and who it affects; link the primary source (release notes, announcement).
Open in the middle of the story at the moment of tension.
Concrete details: dates, tools, numbers, failures, the turning point.
